---
title: "How to predict unit phenotypes from position"
---

The unit encoder describes the **spike-sorted units** you would expect to record at a
position in the brain: their waveform features and the mix of putative cell types they
come from. Like the [spatial encoder](predict-features-from-position.qmd), it takes
positions and returns predictions, at the level of units rather than channels.

| | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| [Spatial encoder](predict-features-from-position.qmd) | Position (`x`, `y`, `z`) | Channel features |
| **Unit encoder** | Position (`x`, `y`, `z`) | Unit waveform features, cell-type composition |

How the model is built is described in [model families](../explanation/model-families.qmd).

## What the model needs

```python
from ephysatlas import load_pretrained

unit = load_pretrained("int-brain-lab/ea-encoder-unit", revision="2026_W42")

print(unit.index["task"])                # unit-encoding
print(unit.index["model_class"])         # UnitAutoencoder
print(unit.inputs["columns"])            # ['x', 'y', 'z']
print(unit.inputs["modalities"])         # ['waveform', 'acg', 'stpc']
print(len(unit.features))                # 10 phenotype features
print(unit.outputs["latent_dim"])        # 60
print(len(unit.subtype_labels))          # 300 sub-types, in 30 types
```

The input is a DataFrame carrying **`x`, `y`, `z` in metres**. Any index works and is
kept; the manifest's own `(pid, cluster)` is the unit tables' index. Positions straight
from `channels.pqt` can be used as they are.

The 10 phenotype features are the waveform features of the
[feature list](../reference/feature-list.qmd) that are defined for a unit's mean waveform:

```python
print(unit.features)
# ['depolarisation_slope', 'recovery_slope', 'repolarisation_slope', 'spatial_spread_um',
#  'tip_val', 'spike_width_secs', 'predepolarisation_width_secs', 'spike_amplitude',
#  'peak_to_trough_ratio_log', 'polarity']
```

## Predict the expected phenotype

```python
import pandas as pd

channels = pd.read_parquet("/data/features/ea_active/2026_W42/agg_full/channels.pqt")
positions = channels.loc[["00a824c0-e060-495f-9ebc-79c82fef4c67"], ["x", "y", "z"]]

pred = unit.predict(positions)
print(pred.shape)          # (384, 10): one row per position
print(pred.columns[:3])    # ['pred_depolarisation_slope', 'pred_recovery_slope', ...]
```

`predict` is deterministic. It mixes each sub-type's expected features with the sub-type
weights at that position, which is what the published unit-level atlas maps show. The
`pred_` prefix keeps a join onto observed features free of collisions.

## Putative cell-type composition

```python
w_type = unit.mixture_weights(positions, level="type")
w_sub = unit.mixture_weights(positions, level="subtype")

print(w_type.shape)            # (384, 30):  type_0 ... type_29
print(w_sub.shape)             # (384, 300): subtype_0.0 ... subtype_29.9
print(w_type.sum(axis=1))      # 1.0 for every position
print(w_type.idxmax(axis=1))   # the dominant type at each position
```

A sub-type `k.j` always lies inside type `k`: the mixture is hierarchical, and assignment
is top-down.

## Draw units

`sample` draws real training units from the same predictive distribution: a sub-type
from the local weights, then one of its training members.

```python
draws = unit.sample(positions.head(3), n_samples=4, seed=0)
print(draws.shape)               # (12, 13): 4 draws for each of 3 positions
print(list(draws.columns[:3]))   # ['sample', 'type', 'subtype'], then the 10 features
```

Each position's label is repeated once per draw. `subtype` indexes
`unit.subtype_labels`. The draws average to `predict`.

## Your own units: latents and assignment

The other direction takes **units**, not positions. `encode` embeds a unit's waveform, 3D
autocorrelogram and population coupling into the 60-D latent. `posterior` and `assign`
place latents in the mixture:

```python
latents = unit.encode(waveform, acg=acg, stpc=stpc)   # (n_units, 60)
types, subtypes = unit.assign(latents)                # top-down hard assignment
```

The inputs must be prepared as for training: max-abs normalised multi-channel waveforms
with the shape the model's config records. `unit.latent_dims(...)` selects the latent
dimensions of a subset of modalities, e.g. for units without population coupling. See the
[`UnitEncoder` API](../api/models.unit_encoder.UnitEncoder.qmd) for every argument,
together with `components()`, `split()` and `preprocessing_stats()`.

## Verify the install

```python
unit.selftest()
# True
```

The self-test reproduces the golden outputs the release ships: phenotype predictions at
500 positions, and the latents of 16 synthetic units. It needs no IBL data access.
